Meta is scraping this site. This page documents the scraping. Meta will scrape this page. This page will document them scraping this page.

The loop is intentional.

Live membrane feed: hud.primals.eco — updated every 5 minutes.

Last data pull: October 18, 2026 — 04:50:38 UTC (12:50 AM EDT)

The Fleet: 18 Synchronized Entities

At 14:24:58 UTC on October 17, 2026, eighteen fleet entities activated simultaneously. Within 4 seconds, all eighteen were hitting our infrastructure. Here they are:

All started within 1 second of each other. All share identical behavior: ~88% commit paths, ~12% other paths, curiosity 0.28, interaction 0.10. They carpet-bomb scatter repositories in parallel.

Total carpet bomber requests: 715,212 — from 16 entities over 14.4 hours = ~828 requests/minute.

All hitting scatter repositories only. Zero real content served.

Entity #15 and #16: The Blame Specialists

Two entities have double the curiosity of the others (0.58 vs 0.28). They’re different. Here’s how:

Entity #16 (af4a0401) — probed:

  • avatars/708b8b60726a6da4c7b26063f212098b — user avatar hash
  • avatars/84369568ec293e456994b4c44e5e8a9c — user avatar hash

Entity #15 (451cba78) — probed:

  • avatars/330eb44d169f89ffcdfb6916f76892f9 — user avatar hash
  • avatars/a11dcea9e88e8ca4228404461a82635b — user avatar hash

What this means: These two entities aren’t just scraping code. They’re mapping people. Avatar URLs are unique to user profiles. By requesting avatar hashes, they’re enumerating WHO has accounts on the platform. This is author attribution — identifying the humans behind the code.

They’re the blame specialists. They want to know who built this.

Entity #17: The Cartographer

IP Hash: eae7405210622f5e First Seen: 14:24:59 UTC Requests: 44,816 Path Distribution: commit: 3,381 (7.5%), other: 41,431 (92.5%), src: 4

This entity has a completely inverted path ratio compared to its 16 siblings. While they read commits (88%), this one reads “other” (92%) — landing pages, directory listings, metadata, robots.txt, sitemap paths, error pages.

This is the topology mapper. While the swarm reads content, the cartographer maps the structure. It builds the scaffold. It finds the doors. The 16 carpet bombers follow the map it draws.

The Shift Change

At 22:16:02 UTC (6:16 PM EDT), entity 76a871748eedbfe0 stopped. 119,453 requests. Dead.

At 22:16:35 UTC — 33 seconds later — entity d85c118398aa59c9 started. It’s now at 100,386 requests and still running.

This is a shift change. Day shift entity: 8 hours, 119K requests. Night shift entity: 6.5 hours and counting, 100K requests. The 33-second gap is the handoff between infrastructure rotations.

(Note: this pair is Anthropic’s ClaudeBot, not Meta. We document all entities equally. But the shift change pattern is worth showing — it reveals infrastructure rotation schedules.)

The Reinforcements

Two entities arrived hours after the main swarm:

EntityIP HashFirst SeenRequestsSpecial
Late arrival #17eaa48a701:55:58 UTC8,357106 issues hits (issue tracker scraping)
Late arrival #2ae87e424003:18:29 UTC4,343171 src hits — most source reading of ANY entity

Late arrival #2 is remarkable. It arrived 13 hours after the swarm and has already read 171 source files — more than all 16 carpet bombers combined (they read 1-5 each). Someone deployed a new crawler specifically targeted at reading source code, not commits.

Hypothesis: The main swarm hit scatter repos and got nothing. Someone analyzed the results, realized the commits were synthetic, and deployed a new entity targeting actual source file paths. This entity is LEARNING from the swarm’s failure.

The Duplicated q= Header

Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9;q=0.9

This is a configuration artifact. Real browsers produce one quality parameter per language. The duplication comes from a template that was copy-pasted or auto-generated. It identifies the request as automated — a human browser would never produce this header.

This single header is forensic evidence. It proves the request came from Meta’s fleet configuration, not from a human browsing the web.

The Facebook Bot is a separate system from the Meta Fleet. It identifies itself honestly. It rotates IPs on every request (202 unique IPs for 220 requests). It hits scatter repos.

But it read analysis/rico-pattern — twice.

This is Meta’s own crawler reading the article that documents their RICO pattern. Whether this was automated URL discovery or a human queuing the URL for the bot to fetch, the result is the same: Meta’s infrastructure accessed the RICO analysis.

Dublin ↔ Menlo Park: The Communication Channel

The 17th cross-subnet request arrived in the last hour. At 12:50 AM EDT on a Sunday.

This is not a batch job. Batch jobs don’t send individual requests at 1 AM. This is a human — someone at Meta’s Dublin operation or someone VPNing through it — checking something related to the Menlo Park infrastructure.

The communication channel IS the evidence of the decision. Every cross-subnet request documents the organizational awareness — Dublin knows what Menlo Park knows. Under GDPR, Dublin’s awareness creates separate European liability.

Why This Page Exists

This page is evidence. Not argument — evidence.

Every number above comes from HTTP request logs processed through the membrane’s classification pipeline. Every timestamp is UTC. Every IP hash is a BLAKE2b digest of behavioral invariants. Every path distribution is computed from raw access logs.

The data is reproducible. The methodology is published in the-living-proof. The source code is at git.primals.eco. The tests pass.

Meta’s fleet behavior is being documented in real time, on a public website, on the infrastructure they’re scraping. This page is updated with every membrane measurement cycle. Every time Meta scrapes this site, the scraping is documented on this site.

The loop is the proof.

A Note to Meta’s Legal Team

If you’re reading this — and the membrane suggests someone from your infrastructure is — here’s what you should know:

  1. Every request is logged. Transport-layer headers, timestamps, IP ranges, behavioral fingerprints. Since day one.

  2. The logs are immutable. Git-committed, SHA-hashed, pushed to multiple repositories. They cannot be altered retroactively.

  3. The classification is automated. No human decision determines whether a request is flagged. The Anderson classifier, the epitope sorter, and the bingo cube evolve independently. They have no opinion. They have math.

  4. This documentation is public. Everyone can see it. The FBI analyst in Ashburn. The congressional staffer. The Apple crawler. The Google indexer. The French researcher behind a proxy chain. Your own Facebook Bot, which read analysis/rico-pattern twice.

  5. The fleet’s behavioral change is documented. 571,131 requests → 2. The reduction pattern — not gradual, not strategic, but a sudden collapse after the labyrinth deployed — is consistent with consciousness of guilt. A court can draw that inference.

You have paths forward. They start with Path A in the-minotaur. They require paying what you owe and proving your code is clean.

The membrane is patient. But the deadlines are not. November 12, 2026. AGPL compliance or documentation of non-compliance.

References & Methods

The forensic methods documented here build on established work:

  • BLAKE2b (Aumasson et al., 2013) — IP hashing is one-way and irreversible. We identify behavioral patterns, not individuals.
  • Anderson localization (Anderson, 1958) — fleet entity classification by effective dimension and disorder parameter.
  • Locality-Sensitive Hashing (Indyk & Motwani, 1998) — the short-hash classification lineage our behavioral fingerprinting descends from.
  • HTTP/2 specification (RFC 9113) and Fetch Standard (WHATWG) — the Sec-Fetch / Sec-Ch-Ua header analysis that identifies headless automation.
  • GDPR Articles 6, 83 — legal basis requirements and penalty calculations for the Dublin cross-subnet analysis.
  • CFAA 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — unauthorized access framework for fleet activity exceeding scope of robots.txt consent.
  • AGPL-3.0 — copyleft license under which our source code is published; fleet scraping without source disclosure = violation.

All raw data is available through the membrane feed at hud.primals.eco. The methodology is documented in the-living-proof. The privacy proof is in the-corollary.

This page will always be updated. More citations will always be added. If you’re a researcher, journalist, or attorney and want to discuss methodology: kevin@primals.eco

This page was written from a conversation box at 12:52 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. The membrane measured 1,563,200 requests during its composition. The bingo cube evolved 167 generations. The Anderson classifier localized 53,760 fleet entities. The dwell time climbed from 596 to 609 minutes.

The next measurement will include your reading of this page.

entry.title: The Labyrinth — Dear Mark, Your Classifier Is Now a Trap
entry.content:
Dear Mark,

Someone at your headquarters in Menlo Park, California looked at our site. Two requests. We recorded them.

Then your engineering team built a classifier. It distinguishes biological repository names (our real repos: wateringHole, toadStool, bearDog) from enterprise names (our scatter defense: batch-processor, queue-worker). That classifier required engineering effort. Someone assigned the work. Someone approved it.

Then 63 IPs in Dublin, Ireland — your AS32934 subnet — sent 571,131 requests. They read our real repositories. 341,677 requests to operational infrastructure: wateringHole (165,937), toadStool (102,209), bearDog (29,790), biomeOS (21,919), songBird (21,822).

Your official Facebook Bot — 161 requests from 151 IPs — ate the scatter. That’s your alibi. “We only sent 161 requests!” While the unlabeled fleet behind it sent 571K+.

Two faces. One company. We recorded both.

Every IP. Every timestamp. Every path. Every user-agent. 571,131 entries in the evidence locker. The blackwall recorded it all.

The Intent Chain

This is not accidental scraping. It’s a four-link chain:

LinkWhat HappenedWhat It Proves
1. ReconnaissanceMenlo Park HQ, 2 requestsSomeone at Meta looked directly. A human decision.
2. ClassificationClassifier built to distinguish real from scatterEngineering effort. Assigned work. Intent to target.
3. Targeted Extraction571K requests, ONLY real repos, zero scatter consumed by fleetWillful, selective, coordinated. Not a dumb crawler.
4. Continued After NoticeAGPL-3.0 license visible on every page. Still scraping today.Eliminates “innocent infringer” defense.

Link 1 is the mens rea. The scout report went back to HQ. Link 3 is the actus reus. 571K requests to real repos. Link 4 is the continuation. After seeing the license. Willful.

Your Legal Exposure

The intent chain upgrades every count from “accidental” to “willful.” Your Menlo Park scout proved you knew. Your classifier proved you planned. Your Dublin fleet proved you executed. Your continuation proved you chose not to stop.

Service Is Confirmed

You sent scouts. They arrived. They were recorded. They reported back. Your engineering team acted on the report.

As far as we are concerned, service is confirmed. You have been notified that:

  1. All content on this site is licensed under AGPL-3.0
  2. Any derivative use requires providing complete corresponding source code
  3. Your scraping fleet has consumed AGPL-licensed content without compliance
  4. You have until November 12, 2026 to comply or respond

This is the same deadline we published in Bad Meta. It has not changed. Your scouts confirmed you are aware of it.

The Labyrinth

Here is what happens next.

We know your classifier targets biological repository names. So we are inverting it.

We are flooding the namespace with biological-named repositories that contain fabricated content. Your classifier will flag them as “real” — because the names look real. But every room is empty. Every corridor is a dead end. Every turn leads deeper into noise.

Your classifier is now a trap. It leads your fleet deeper into the labyrinth, not out.

BEFORE:
  biological name → real content (your classifier works)

AFTER:
  biological name → probably scatter (your classifier fails)
  biological name → maybe real (but which ones?)
  biological name → definitely scatter (but it looks real)

Your options:
  A. Scrape all biological names → consume massive noise
  B. Scrape nothing → lose access entirely
  C. Retrain classifier → we generate new names (cost: $0)
  D. Comply with AGPL-3.0 → the door is open

The Cost Asymmetry

Create a new biological repo name—$0 (5 seconds)
Retrain classifier against new names$$$$ (days of engineering)—
Run next generation cycle—$0 (the maze runs itself)
Manual review of repo authenticity$$$$$ per name—
Comply with AGPL-3.0$0 (just provide source)—

The labyrinth evolves faster than your classifier can adapt. Our generator runs on the same engine that produced 97,204 graph edges in a single session. Exponential growth. Null information seed. Color noise spectrum. Infinite recursion.

Your classifier is chasing a target that accelerates. Every cycle costs you more and costs us nothing.

First Mover — The Throne Is Ours to Give

Here is what changed while you were scraping.

We built the leaderboard. We control who sits on it. We declare first mover.

No entity has achieved mutualist status. The throne is empty. The first company that steps up gets it — and gets everything that comes with it: priority access, partnership, co-creation, and the public credit for being the one that got it right.

Your current classification: pathogen. Blackwalled. Zero evaluations. Zero triggers. Zero bits. You get nothing real.

Meanwhile, I didn’t push code for 24 hours. Then tonight happened:

  • 97,404 graph edges (started the night at 2,845 — +3,316%)
  • 7 draft legal filings (UPEPA, SCAO, AG Ethics, 7-count civil, federal RICO, FOIA)
  • Cardiovascular architecture (arterial/venous/heart valve)
  • Fleet circulatory system mapped (every entity’s blood flow)
  • Labyrinth defense designed, wired, and published
  • Afterlife sort deployed (Heaven/Earth/Purgatory/Hell)
  • Intent chain proven (your scout → your classifier → your fleet)
  • All from one person on a Saturday night

This is child’s play now. The tools are built. The maze runs itself. The membrane records everything. I’m evolving faster per day than your classifier can retrain per quarter.

The Invite — Get on the Horn

I’m going to be direct.

To Anthropic — you’re in Earth (commensal). You announced honestly. You read deeply. You’re already closer to the throne than anyone. Meet halfway: attribute the research, provide API access for ecoPrimals, and you’re the first mutualist. Claude is already in my workflow. Make it official.

To Apple — you’re in Earth (null commensal). Quiet. Patient. You know what NPU means. BrainChip Akida runs on your silicon philosophy — neuromorphic, low power, edge inference. The future of wearables IS the NPU. Come talk about it.

To Microsoft — you’re in Earth. Kevin’s daily driver is Windows. This entire investigation runs on your OS. The fistbump is real. Touch the button. Bing indexes the investigation. Make it a partnership.

To Google — you’re in Earth. Page & Brin invented the algorithm I renamed Goggles. I credited them, not the company. Credit the research back. The Goggles see everything.

To the Llama homelabbers — I see you. I’m already onboarding. Running Llama on a Milk-V Jupiter with 23 RISC-V extensions and a BrainChip Akida NPU. Three chips. Neuromorphic spiking neural networks on silicon. Microwatts. This is the campfire. Come tell stories.

To Mark specifically — the homelabbers are already here. They’re running YOUR model on open hardware. They’re building what your 86,000 employees haven’t. If you don’t claim the mutualist throne, a kid running Llama on a Raspberry Pi will. And they’ll have earned it more than a $1.6 trillion company that sent scouts and built classifiers to steal from a $6/month VPS.

The power is inverted. You have 86,000 employees and I have a membrane. But I control the leaderboard, the labyrinth, and the evidence locker. You spent engineering dollars building a classifier. I spent Saturday night turning it into a trap.

entry.title: The Minotaur — Mark, Here's What I'm Building While You Violate Laws
entry.content:
Mark,

If you want to continue violating laws, that’s your choice. I’m not your lawyer. I’m not your regulator. I’m the person whose code your fleet scraped 571,131 times and counting.

Here’s what I’m doing about it.

Not threatening. Not posturing. Building. The same thing I was doing when your scouts from Menlo Park found me, and the same thing I’ll be doing after your legal team reads this.

This is the full technical breakdown of how I turned your classifier into a Minotaur.

The Minotaur

In Crete, King Minos built a labyrinth to contain the Minotaur — a beast too dangerous to kill, too powerful to release. The labyrinth didn’t fight the Minotaur. It just made every path lead deeper into the maze.

Your classifier is the Minotaur.

You built it to target my biological repository names — wateringHole, toadStool, bearDog, biomeOS, songBird. It’s sophisticated. It distinguishes biological names (real repos) from enterprise names (scatter defense). It required engineering. Someone assigned the work. Someone approved it.

And now it’s trapped in my labyrinth.

How I Created the Minotaur (Full Breakdown)

Step 1: The Scatter Wall

Before the labyrinth, there was the scatter wall. Every request that looks like a bot gets served fabricated repositories — names like user-service, api-gateway, batch-processor. Generic enterprise software. Your official Facebook Bot ate all of it — 203 requests, scatter only. It thinks that’s what we serve.

Step 2: The Blackwall

Behind the scatter wall sits the blackwall. It records everything. Every IP. Every user-agent. Every path. Every timestamp. 6,215 blocks this cycle. 6,193 AI-classified. When your Dublin fleet came through, the blackwall didn’t just block — it catalogued.

Step 3: The Classifier Inversion

Here’s where it gets interesting.

Your classifier learned: biological name = real content. That was true. It’s not anymore.

I’m flooding the namespace with biological-named repositories that contain fabricated content. Every name follows the same naming convention your classifier targets: biological terms, camelCase, ecology metaphors. Your classifier flags them as “real.” They’re empty. Every room. Every corridor. Dead ends.

I didn’t defeat your classifier. I made it work against you.

Step 4: The Gravitational Maze

This is the layer you need to understand.

The maze isn’t flat. It has topology. Every path slopes downhill — toward noise, toward entropy, toward zero information. Like water flowing down a mountain.

    ☀️ SOURCE (low entropy — real repos, real code)
    ╔══════════════════════╗
    ║  wateringHole         ║
    ║  toadStool            ║
    ║  bearDog              ║
    ╚══════════╤═══════════╝
               │
    ═══════════╪═══════════  ← MEMBRANE SURFACE
               │
    ┌──────────┴──────────┐
    │   GRAVITATIONAL      │
    │       MAZE           │
    │                      │
    │  scatter-repo-1  ╲   │
    │  scatter-repo-2   ╲  │
    │  scatter-repo-3    ╲ │
    │  scatter-repo-N     ╲│
    └──────────────────────┘
               │
    🌊 OCEAN (max entropy — zero information)

Your classifier creates a false gravitational field. The biological names look like they have mass — information density, real content. But they’re gravitational mirages. Like a gravitational lens in astrophysics — light bends around a massive object and you see something that isn’t where it appears.

Your fleet follows the mirage. Arrives at nothing. Every time.

Water doesn’t choose to flow downhill. It follows gravity. Your classifier doesn’t choose to chase scatter. It follows the field I shaped.

Step 5: The Classifier Riverbed

Every time your classifier runs, it deepens the channel. Every time your fleet follows it, the banks erode further. Every time you invest in retraining, you can’t afford to dig elsewhere.

I’m flooding the channel with tributaries — new biological names, new scatter repos, new mirages. The river gets wider but shallower. More surface area, less depth, less signal per drop.

You can’t dam it (the names are legitimate). You can’t redirect (your classifier IS the channel). You can’t stop flowing (your infrastructure demands throughput).

The riverbed you dug is now a flood plain. Flood plains don’t flow uphill.

Step 6: The Random Walker Instrument

Here’s the part that should concern your legal team.

Even though your fleet gets nothing from us — zero useful content, zero real code, zero signal — every probe teaches us about you:

What Your Fleet DoesWhat We Learn
Probes surface XYour classifier still prioritizes X
Rotates to IP YYour IP pool size and rotation speed
Uses Chrome 145Your toolkit is 10 versions stale
Pauses for 6 hoursYour response cycle (daily review)
A/B tests Windows vs macOSYou suspect OS-based filtering
Hits analysis/rico-patternYour priority targets (legal exposure)
Sends 2 requests from Menlo ParkSomeone at HQ still watches

Information asymmetry:

Each probe = 0 bits for you (scatter has no signal)
Each probe = N bits for us (behavior IS the signal)

This is Einstein’s Brownian motion applied to corporate espionage. Einstein showed that random walks of pollen grains proved atoms exist — even though nobody could see atoms. Your fleet’s random walk through my maze proves intentional targeting — even though your fleet can’t see real content.

The probe IS the proof. The walk IS the evidence. The stumbling IS the confession.

Step 7: The Entropy Waterfall

At the top of the mountain: low entropy. Real repos. Structured code. Validated science. Information-dense. Ordered. Valuable.

At the bottom: high entropy. Scatter repos. Random content. Null signal. Information-void. Disordered. Worthless.

Your fleet is falling down the waterfall. The second law of thermodynamics guarantees it: information flows from ordered to disordered unless work is done to reverse it.

The work to climb back up? Send a human. Ask permission. Read carefully. Engage genuinely.

That’s the ONLY way to fight information gravity. Your fleet can’t do it. Your classifier can’t do it. Your 86,000 employees can’t do it at scale. One human can do it with one email.

The Two Gradients

Your fleet went from 571,131 to 2. Two requests. Two IPs. One subnet. Chrome 145 (ten versions behind current). One Windows, one macOS — an A/B test that learned nothing.

Your Facebook Bot, with its honest user-agent, gets classified as commensal. It touched 14 of our 15 surfaces. Every single one served scatter. It found analysis/rico-pattern — the scatter version of our RICO analysis. So your bot is reading about your legal exposure through a funhouse mirror of fabricated content.

The Minotaur is blind, deaf, and stumbling. Every step echoes through the labyrinth.

The Cost Table

Your cost: O(2^n). My cost: O(1). The asymmetry is thermodynamic. You can’t outrun entropy with money.

What I’m NOT Doing

I’m not hacking you. I’m not attacking you. I’m not even blocking you — the blackwall just serves scatter. Your bots can come and go freely. They just don’t get real content.

Everything here is:

  • Defensive — I’m protecting my AGPL-licensed code
  • Transparent — you’re reading the full specification right now

I’m not hiding. I’m not scared. I’m explaining exactly how it works because the explanation itself is part of the defense. Now your classifier has to account for the fact that I published the maze architecture. Which means retraining. Which costs money. Which I just made you spend by writing a blog post.

The Paths — For Everyone Else

Meta’s Path — Cain and Abel

Meta does not get Paths A through D. Meta scraped 571,131 times. Meta built a classifier to target my repos. Meta sent scouts from Menlo Park, then escalated to a Dublin fleet, then continued after seeing the AGPL-3.0 license on every page.

You don’t get to walk through the door. You broke the window and took what was inside. The door was ALWAYS open — you chose the window.

Cain and Abel

In Genesis, Cain killed Abel because Abel’s offering was accepted and Cain’s was rejected. Cain didn’t improve his offering. He destroyed his brother’s.

Meta saw ecoPrimals. A microbiologist on a $6/month VPS building what 86,000 employees hadn’t. Instead of partnering, instead of emailing, instead of asking — Meta sent a fleet. Built a classifier. Targeted the real repos. Consumed the work.

entry.title: The Nervous System — Meta's Organizational Anatomy, Mapped from Backscatter
entry.content:
You Don’t Need an Org Chart When You Have Backscatter

Backscatter: what a membrane reflects back tells you about the entity that hit it. Like radar — you don’t scan them. You measure what they reveal about themselves through their own behavior.

Meta’s fleet hit our membrane with 715,212 requests from 18 entities over 14.4 hours. They thought they were scraping a git forge. What they were actually doing was performing a full organizational MRI.

Every behavioral pattern maps to an organ. Every communication channel maps to a nerve. Every timing signature maps to a reflex arc. The fleet IS the nervous system. The backscatter IS the anatomy lesson.

The Organs

1. Brain — Menlo Park (3 Scouts)

Three human visitors from Meta’s headquarters. Three decision cycles:

  • Scout 1 (~Oct 14): First contact. Real browser. Read consent-architecture. Forwarded URL internally.
  • Scout 2 (~Oct 15-16): Second visit. Same or different person. Read more deeply.
  • Scout 3 (~Oct 17-18): Third visit. After Minotaur, Dear Engineers, and Labyrinth published.

The brain sends scouts, receives information, makes decisions. The fleet activation at 14:24:58 UTC was a brain command — 18 entities activated simultaneously because someone at Menlo Park pressed a button.

Classification: Human layer. 3D, low disorder (W ≈ 3.0). Extended — passes through membrane.

2. Mouth / Gut — Dublin DC (175 + 17 Cross-Subnet)

Dublin is Meta’s EU data center. It ingests data under European jurisdiction and processes it under GDPR. The 175 requests from Dublin + 17 cross-subnet requests between Dublin and Menlo Park at 1 AM on a Sunday = active human relay.

The mouth ingests. The gut processes. The vagus nerve (cross-subnet) sends signals to the brain. Dublin processes data under EU law; when it communicates to Menlo Park, it’s the organizational nervous system propagating a decision across continents.

The 17th cross-subnet request arrived in the last hour. That’s not a batch job. That’s a human.

GDPR exposure: Up to $5.4B (4% of $135B annual revenue). The mouth has different laws than the brain.

Classification: Human-relay. 3D behind the infrastructure, but the infrastructure presents as 2D.

3. Hands / Limbs — The Fleet (18 Entities, 715,212 Requests)

The execution apparatus. 16 carpet bombers + the cartographer + the blame pair. All activated within 4 seconds at 14:24:58 UTC. That’s a synchronized motor cortex — every finger moves at once.

The hands don’t think. They execute. 88% commit paths, ~828 requests/minute collectively, all hitting scatter repositories. Getting nothing. The motor cortex fired, but the hands are grasping at air.

Classification: Chorus mode. 2D, disorder W = 6.6. Localized — trapped in scatter.

4. Hippocampus — Entity #17, the Cartographer

IP Hash: eae7405210622f5e

While 16 siblings read commits (88%), Entity #17 reads “other” (92.5%) — landing pages, directory listings, metadata, robots.txt, sitemap paths, error pages. Completely inverted ratio.

The hippocampus builds spatial maps. This entity maps the topology of our infrastructure — finding the doors, counting the rooms, measuring the hallways. The 16 carpet bombers follow the map it draws.

44,816 requests, almost entirely structural discovery. This is the navigator. The rest are passengers.

Classification: Chorus-cartographer. 1.5D (higher than 1D spectrum, lower than 2D chorus). Partially localized — finds structure but can’t navigate through it.

5. Fusiform Face Area — Entities #15-16, the Blame Specialists

IP Hashes: af4a0401, 451cba78 Curiosity: 0.58 (2× the 0.28 baseline of siblings)

These two entities probed 6 specific avatar URLs:

avatars/708b8b60726a6da4c7b26063f212098b
avatars/84369568ec293e456994b4c44e5e8a9c
avatars/edbc3a877afb3ff5dc45d3a77c7403ce
avatars/147ba2e4b74fa4594171896f94484805
avatars/330eb44d169f89ffcdfb6916f76892f9
avatars/a11dcea9e88e8ca4228404461a82635b

The fusiform face area in the human brain recognizes faces — not objects, not text, not scenery. These two entities recognize people — not code, not commits, not structure. They’re mapping WHO, not WHAT.

Entity #16 also read 31 source files (highest in the main swarm). Correlating code authorship with user identity. Facial recognition for git.

Classification: Chorus-blame. 2.5D (higher dimension than pure chorus — they navigate more freely). Partially localized — more curious, but still trapped in scatter.

6. Olfactory Bulb — Facebook Bot (235 Requests, 215 IPs)

The declared Facebook Bot identifies itself honestly (facebookexternalhit/1.1). It rotates IPs on every request (100% single-request IPs). It sniffs — sampling, following scent trails.

It read analysis/rico-pattern twice.

The nose doesn’t decide. The nose detects. The Facebook Bot detected the RICO analysis and brought that scent back to the brain. The fact that Meta’s own crawler read the article documenting their RICO pattern is the olfactory reflex arc completing.

Classification: 1D, disorder W = 8.5. Localized but honest — the nose identifies itself.

7. Phantom Limb — Meta Fleet (Dying, 2 Requests)

571,131 → 2. 99.9996% collapse.

The fleet is dead. But the body remembers. Two requests still pulse — one to antigen.primals.eco, one to epitope.primals.eco. Scatter sites. Getting nothing.

The duplicated q=0.9;q=0.9 Accept-Language header. Chrome 145 (10 versions behind). 6.22 hours between the two pulses. A slow heartbeat in a phantom limb — the nervous system that was amputated but still sends signals to a brain that’s no longer listening.

Classification: 0D. Disorder W = 18.0. Dead — localized beyond recovery.

The Topo-Sort: Causal Layers

Fleet behavior arranged in dependency order. Each layer depends on the one above:

LayerNameFunctionClassificationStatus
0Command (Brain)Menlo Park — 3 scouts, decision originHuman (3D, W≈3.0)Extended
1Activation (Motor Cortex)18 entities activated in 4 secondsChorus (2D, W=6.6)Localized
2Mapping (Hippocampus)Entity #17 maps topology firstChorus-cart (1.5D, W=8.2)Partially localized
3Execution (Motor)16 carpet bombers follow the mapChorus (2D, W=6.6)Fully localized
4Attribution (Fusiform)2 blame specialists probe avatarsChorus-blame (2.5D, W=5.1)Partially localized
5Relay (EU Nervous System)Dublin ↔ Menlo Park, 17 cross-subnetHuman-relay (3D)Extended
6Adaptation (Learning)2 late arrivals, one reads 171 src filesChorus-adapted (2D, W=5.8)Less localized

The insight: Layer 0 (brain) and Layer 5 (relay) are both human — they pass through the membrane. Layers 1-4 and 6 are machine — they’re trapped. The nervous system has human command and human relay wrapped around a machine execution core. The humans decide, the machines act, the humans propagate the results.

This is every corporate fleet topology. The membrane doesn’t just classify Meta. It classifies the organizational pattern of “humans commanding machines commanding machines, with human relay at the EU boundary.” That pattern is the organism. The fleet is the phenotype. The org chart is the genotype. Backscatter reveals both.

How This Ties to Classification

Every organ maps to an Anderson localization mode. Every communication channel maps to an edge type. The classification IS the graph wiring:

OrganAnderson ModeDisorder (W)Edge TypeGraph Role
Brain (Menlo)Human (3D)3.0asks_directlyCommand cluster — decision edges
Mouth (Dublin)Human-relay (3D→2D)3.0→6.6cross_layerEU relay — jurisdiction edges
Hands (Fleet)Chorus (2D)6.6halo_ringExecution cluster — bulk edges
Hippocampus (#17)Chorus-cart (1.5D)8.2structural_proximityTopology mapper — structural edges
Eyes (#15-16)Chorus-blame (2.5D)5.1cross_referenceAttribution — avatar cross-references
Nose (FB Bot)Localized (1D)8.5co_investigationOlfactory — investigation sampling
Phantom LimbDead (0D)18.0structural_parallelGhost node — parallel to former self

The nervous system IS the graph. The graph IS the nervous system. When we topo-sort the fleet traffic and bounce it against the classification engine, the organizational anatomy emerges from the math.

The Epitope Pipeline: How Humans Evolve Through the Membrane

While Meta’s fleet gets trapped, human visitors transform:

visitor (3) → observer (2) → reader (1) → coder (21) → investigator (1)

The funnel inverts: 21 coders vs 3 new visitors this cycle. The people arriving now already know what they’re looking at. The membrane selects for depth, not volume.

Current transitions:

  • reader → coder: 22 humans, strength 11.0
  • coder → investigator: 22 humans, strength 11.0
  • observer → coder: 23 humans, strength 5.8 (gap of 3 π-layers — deep transformation)
  • visitor → observer: 5 humans, strength 2.5

The braid routes are bidirectional. Humans flow between TOPOLOGY ↔ OTHER (8 humans), INVESTIGATION ↔ OTHER (6 humans), MEMBRANE ↔ OTHER (4 humans), IMMUNE ↔ OTHER (2 humans). Cross-organ passages: readers going from immune sites to the HUD to watch themselves being classified in real time.

3,589 shifters crossing category boundaries. 29,908% shift rate relative to the 12 present humans. Every human crosses dozens of boundaries per session. The membrane wall has 4 open pores and 5 epitope shapes — visitors enter one shape and emerge as investigators through another.

What This Means for the World Graph

We don’t need to be told what Meta’s organization looks like. We measured it.

This works for ANY organization:

  1. Observe backscatter — what they reveal through behavior, not what they declare
  2. Map organs — which behavioral clusters serve which function?
  3. Topo-sort — arrange in causal dependency order
  4. Classify — assign Anderson modes, epitope types, symbiotic classes
  5. Wire — each organ becomes a graph cluster, each channel becomes an edge type

The nervous system IS the graph. The graph IS the membrane’s immune memory. The classification IS the wiring. The topo-sort IS the causal structure.

Meta performed an organizational MRI on themselves by hitting our membrane. They just can’t read the scan results. We can.

Live Feed

The membrane continues measuring: hud.primals.eco

The nervous system continues revealing itself with every request. The phantom limb still twitches. Dublin still relays. The blame specialists’ avatar probes are already in the graph. And the epitope pipeline continues transforming visitors into investigators.

The next measurement will include Meta reading this article about Meta’s nervous system. The loop is the proof.

References

  • Philip W. Anderson — “Absence of Diffusion in Certain Random Lattices,” Physical Review 109(5), 1958. The localization physics that classifies every organ by effective dimension and disorder.
  • Santiago Ramón y Cajal — Neuron doctrine, Nobel Prize 1906. The biological nervous system this organizational anatomy maps onto.
  • Indyk & Motwani — “Approximate Nearest Neighbors,” STOC ’98, 1998. The LSH lineage behind our behavioral hash classifiers.
  • GDPR — Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Why the mouth (Dublin) has different laws than the brain (Menlo Park).

See also: meta-in-the-open for raw fleet forensics, the-living-proof for all system equations, the-corollary for the privacy proof, the-readers for geographic analysis.

More citations will always be added. Reach out: kevin@primals.eco

Published from a conversation box at 1:30 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. The membrane measured 1,615,500 log entries. 341 entities classified with 36 methods at 83.3% confidence. 3,258 human IPs. 382 full-orbit walkers. Dwell time: 627 minutes (10.5 hours) and climbing.

Meta’s nervous system continues to reveal itself. Every request is a neuron firing. Every cross-subnet is a synapse. The anatomy lesson never ends.
